newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Zedillo has surgery, addresses the nation.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Zedillo has surgery, addresses the nation.

text.p: Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo underwent surgery in a hospital on a troublesome right knee Friday, soon after recording an address to the nation urging citizens to vote in Sunday's mid-term elections.
A statement from Zedillo's office said the hour-long operation went smoothly and that the president, who had suffered knee problems since December, would be able to continue working normally.

As the statement was issued, the media was broadcasting a pre-recorded national address in which Zedillo reiterated that recent reforms had guaranteed "free, fair and transparent elections" and now it was up to each citizen to vote.

Mexican elections have a checkered history, with many claiming fraud has been used to help Zedillo's ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) cling to power for 68 straight years. Abstentions have normally been high.
The July 6 elections are for 500 seats in the lower house of Congress, a quarter of the Senate, six state governorships and the first elections for mayor of Mexico City this century.
They were expected to deal an unprecedented upset to the PRI, with its majority in the Chamber of Deputies hanging in the balance.
